Operator: Good day, and welcome to the GlobalCom Inc. Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Instructions for queuing your questions will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to GlobalCom Inc.'s Q3 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Maria Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Network Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report our results for Q3. We exceeded expectations in several key areas. First, we delivered strong service revenue growth across our wireless, broadband, and enterprise segments. Second, our churn rates continued to trend favorably, reflecting the strength of our customer retention strategies. Third, free cash flow generation was robust, supporting our capital allocation priorities. Fourth, our commitment to shareholder returns remains unwavering, with sustainable dividends and buybacks. Finally, we are strategically advancing our network investments, particularly in 5G deployment.

We're seeing very positive results from our investments in 5G advanced services, and their impact on ARPU and customer satisfaction is significant. We focused on operational excellence amid competitive pressures, and our balanced approach is proving successful.

Maria Chen: Thank you, Alex. Turning to the financials, our revenue for the quarter was $24.5 billion, up 7.2% year-over-year. Our adjusted EBITDA was $10.4 billion, resulting in a margin of 42.5%. We are maintaining strict cost discipline. Capital expenditures were $5.2 billion, primarily allocated to 5G rollout and fiber expansion.

Good afternoon, everyone—though it's morning here, thank you for joining our Q3 earnings call for GlobalCom Inc. I'll now dive into our service revenue performance, which totaled $14.7 billion for the quarter, up 5.8% year-over-year on a reported basis and 6.2% on a constant-currency basis. This marks our 11th straight quarter of service revenue growth, underscoring the resilience of our core wireless, broadband, and enterprise segments amid a dynamic macroeconomic environment. Let me break it down segment by segment, highlighting the year-over-year percentage changes, key drivers, and our strategic initiatives.

Starting with wireless, which remains our largest revenue contributor at about 60% of total service revenues. We delivered 4.2% year-over-year growth to $8.9 billion, accelerating from 3.7% in Q2, driven by a combination of subscriber net adds, ARPU expansion, and 5G monetization.

Postpaid service revenues grew 5.1% year-over-year to $7.2 billion, fueled by 1.2 million postpaid phone net adds—our strongest quarterly performance since Q4 2022. This was powered by our Ultra5G network, which now covers 95% of our U.S. population footprint and 85% in Europe following our recent spectrum acquisitions in the 3.5 GHz CBRS and n78 bands. 5G Standalone subscribers surged 28% year-over-year to 45 million, enabling premium features like network slicing for gaming and XR applications, which boosted postpaid ARPU by 2.3% to $52.40. We're seeing early traction with our 5G Advanced bundles, including partnerships with Apple for satellite SOS integration and Epic Games for cloud gaming latency under 10ms.

Prepaid grew a more modest 1.8% year-over-year to $1.4 billion, reflecting competitive pressures from discount MVNOs like Visible and Mint Mobile. However, our value-focused ConnectMore plans, with unlimited 5G data at $25/month, stemmed churn to just 0.9%—industry-leading—and added 450,000 net adds.

Regionally, U.S. wireless grew 5.5% year-over-year, outpacing Verizon's reported 3.9% thanks to our mid-band 5G leadership. In Europe, growth was 2.1% amid regulatory headwinds in Germany, but our Vodafone joint venture is ramping Open RAN deployments to cut opex by 15%. Latin America lagged at 1.5% due to FX volatility in Brazil, offset by 4G LTE expansions in underserved markets.

Strategically, we're investing $2.1 billion in capex this year for 5G SA core upgrades and dynamic spectrum sharing, positioning us for 6G R&D pilots with Nokia and Qualcomm by 2026.

Broadband was the star performer, surging 8.5% year-over-year—more than double the industry average per Dell'Oro Group data—reaching $3.8 billion. This reflects our aggressive fiber and hybrid-fiber-coax investments amid surging demand for hybrid work and streaming.

Residential broadband revenues climbed 9.2% year-over-year to $3.1 billion, with 850,000 net adds, including 450,000 fiber customers. Our FiberFast network now passes 35 million locations, up 22% year-over-year, with take rates hitting 52%—up from 47% a year ago—thanks to gigabit symmetrical speeds at $70/month. In competitive markets like the U.S. Sun Belt, we're gaining share from cable peers like Comcast's Xfinity, where our 2 Gbps offers undercut their pricing by 10%. Fixed Wireless Access added 250,000 subscribers via mmWave spectrum, capturing rural demand and competing effectively with T-Mobile's FWA and emerging Starlink satellite broadband.

Video revenues within broadband grew 3.5% year-over-year to $650 million, defying cord-cutting trends through skinny bundles like StreamHub, which integrates Netflix, Disney+, and our ad-supported AVOD tier for $45/month. Churn held at 1.1%, below the 1.6% U.S. industry average per Leichtman Research.

Internationally, Europe broadband jumped 12% year-over-year post our Liberty Global acquisition synergies, with DOCSIS 4.0 upgrades delivering 10 Gbps downstream in the UK and Netherlands. Asia-Pacific was flat at 0.5% due to saturated markets in Japan, but we're piloting XGS-PON fiber with NTT.

Our $1.8 billion broadband capex this year targets 50 million fiber passings by 2026, with RROI projected at 25%+, leveraging BEAD funding in the U.S. and Gigabit Voucher programs in Europe.

Enterprise rounded out the quarter with solid 6.1% year-over-year growth to $2.0 billion, beating our guidance midpoint and reflecting strength in high-margin connectivity and managed services.

Wireless enterprise revenues rose 7.8% year-over-year, driven by IoT and private 5G networks. We added 1.5 million IoT lines, up 35% year-over-year, with deployments for logistics giants like UPS using our Low-Power Wide-Area on NB-IoT. Private 5G Standalone sites grew to 2,500, serving manufacturing verticals with URLLC latency under 1ms—think BMW plants in Europe mirroring Verizon's pilots.

Wireline enterprise grew 4.9% year-over-year, led by SD-WAN and edge computing. Our GlobalNet SD-WAN platform, powered by VMware integration, secured 400 new wins, including a $150 million multi-year deal with a Fortune 50 retailer for SASE security. Cloud Connect revenues hit $450 million, up 15%, bundling direct AWS and Azure interconnects with our 400G Ethernet backbone.

Regionally, North America drove 7.2% growth amid hyperscaler demand, while EMEA was 4.5% boosted by 5G campus networks in Germany under the Gaia-X initiative. APAC grew 5.0%, tempered by China slowdowns but offset by enterprise 5G slicing for Singapore Smart Nation projects.

Strategically, we're allocating $800 million in enterprise capex for edge data centers and AI-optimized orchestration via our Cisco and Ericsson partnerships. This positions us for 10%+ CAGR through 2027, as enterprises shift from MPLS to 5G/SD-WAN hybrids.

In summary, our service revenue growth of 5.8% year-over-year demonstrates balanced execution across segments, with broadband leading and wireless/enterprise providing stability. We're on track for full-year service growth of 5.5-6.0%, with adjusted EBITDA margins expanding 50 basis points to 42.5%.

As we dive into our operational metrics, I'd like to spend some time on churn rate analysis, a critical leading indicator for subscriber retention and long-term revenue stability in our telecom and media segments. Churn remains a focal point for us, especially in this hyper-competitive landscape with aggressive pricing from players like T-Mobile and Verizon, ongoing cord-cutting pressures akin to those impacting Comcast and Charter, and the streaming wars heating up with Netflix, Disney+, and our own GlobalStream service.

Let me start with the headline numbers. Our blended monthly churn rate across postpaid mobile, fixed broadband, and video/streaming services came in at 1.12% for Q3, a 15 basis point improvement quarter-over-quarter from 1.27% in Q2, and a robust 220 basis point year-over-year decline from 1.34% in Q3 last year. This marks our lowest blended churn in over three years, reflecting the early payoffs from our $2.5 billion capex ramp in network densification and content investments. On an annualized basis, that's translating to a 13.3% annual churn rate, well below the industry average of 18-20% for diversified telco-media peers.

Breaking it down by segment for more granularity: Postpaid mobile churn at 0.82% monthly in Q3, down 8 basis points quarter-over-quarter and 45 basis points year-over-year. This is elite territory—better than AT&T's reported 0.85% and on par with T-Mobile's industry-leading 0.75%. Net adds here were 450,000, driven by our 5G Ultra Wideband rollout covering 85% of our top 100 markets.

Fixed broadband churn: 1.05% monthly, improved 12 basis points quarter-over-quarter from 1.17%, and 30 basis points year-over-year better. Fiber-to-the-home penetration hit 42% of our base, helping us stem losses to cable rivals like Xfinity.

Video/streaming churn: This remains our highest at 4.2% monthly (annualized ~45%), down from 4.8% quarter-over-quarter but still elevated year-over-year due to seasonal content gaps. GlobalStream lost 120,000 subs net, pressured by Disney+ bundle poaching and free ad-supported TV alternatives like Tubi.

Voluntary churn—comprising 65% of total—fell to 0.73% blended, while involuntary held steady at 0.39%. Our economic churn, factoring in downgrades to lower-ARPU plans, improved to 1.45% annualized, supporting modest ARPU stability at $58.20 blended.

Key trends: We've seen a clear inflection point since Q1 2023. Churn peaked at 1.48% blended amid last year's inflation spike and 5G spectrum auction distractions, but has trended down steadily: 1.42% in Q1 '24, 1.27% Q2, and now 1.12%. This mirrors broader industry stabilization post-COVID mobility surges, but we're outpacing peers—our year-over-year improvement is 2x Verizon's and 1.5x Comcast's, per S&P Global data. Leading into Q4, we expect further compression to sub-1.1% as holiday bundling kicks in.

Primary drivers—positive and negative: On the upside, our technical initiatives are delivering. The 5G Standalone core deployment across 70% of our footprint has boosted network NPS scores by 18 points year-over-year, directly correlating to a 25% reduction in service-related churn. We've also launched AI-driven personalization via our myGlobalCom app, using machine learning to recommend bundles—retaining 15% more at-risk subs through predictive offers like 'Unlimited 5G + GlobalStream for $10/mo add-on.' Content-wise, exclusives like our partnership with Peacock for NFL Sunday Ticket alternatives drove a 30% churn reduction in sports-heavy households. Bundling remains king: 68% of our low-churn base (<0.5% monthly) is on converged mobile-fixed-video plans, echoing success stories at Vodafone in Europe.

Headwinds include macroeconomic sensitivity—voluntary mobile churn spiked 10 basis points in price-elastic regions during our mid-year Unlimited plan repricing—and competitive intensity. T-Mobile's 'Go5G Next' zero-early-termination offers lured 8% of our competitive losses, while broadband poaching by Frontier Fiber rose 22% year-over-year. Streaming churn is exacerbated by 'subscription fatigue,' with 40% of departures citing overlapping services like Hulu + Max bundles.

Regional commentary: North America (75% of subs): Best-in-class at 0.95% blended monthly churn, down 30 basis points year-over-year. US markets like California and Texas benefited from DOCSIS 4.0 upgrades, holding broadband churn under 1%. Canada saw slight uptick to 1.15% from regulatory price caps.

Europe (15% of subs): 1.35% blended, flat quarter-over-quarter but 10 basis points worse year-over-year due to EU roaming caps and energy cost pass-throughs. UK and Germany strong at 1.2% post our Three UK acquisition synergies; Spain challenged at 1.6% from Digi Mobil's low-cost MVNO aggression.

Latin America & APAC (10% of subs): Highest at 1.85% blended, but improving 50 basis points year-over-year on prepaid-to-postpaid conversions. Brazil's 5G auctions enabled 20% churn cuts via Claro partnerships; India remains volatile at 2.4% amid Jio's tariff hikes.

Strategic insights and outlook: Churn is our North Star for lifetime value optimization—every 10 basis points reduction adds ~$150 million to FY25 EBITDA. We're doubling down on zero-touch retention with GenAI chatbots handling 40% of at-risk interactions, targeting 0.05% monthly savings. Expect Q4 catalysts from fiber expansion to 50% coverage and GlobalStream's live sports push, including MLS exclusives. Competitively, we're monitoring Dish Network's 5G pivot and Starlink rural plays, but our urban density moat positions us well.

In summary, churn trends are structurally favorable, driven by tech leadership and sticky bundles. We're guiding to 1.05-1.10% blended for Q4 and 1.08% full-year average, supporting 2.5 million net adds and 3% revenue growth.

Today, I'd like to dive deep into our free cash flow generation and utilization, which remains a cornerstone of our financial strength here at GlobalCom Inc. As you know, in the hyper-competitive telecommunications and media landscape—think the ongoing 5G spectrum auctions reminiscent of Verizon's C-band frenzy or the streaming wars echoing Netflix and Disney's bundle strategies—robust FCF is what fuels both our network dominance and content ecosystem leadership.

For Q3, we delivered free cash flow of $2.8 billion, a robust 18% increase year-over-year and 12% sequentially from Q2. This marks our 11th straight quarter of FCF growth, underscoring the resilience of our hybrid telco-media model. To break it down: operating cash flow came in at $4.5 billion, up 14% year-over-year, driven by a 3.2% rise in wireless service revenues to $12.1 billion, fueled by postpaid ARPU expansion to $52.40—our strongest in two years—thanks to premium 5G Unlimited plans bundled with our GlobalStream SVOD service. Wireline broadband added $1.8 billion, with FWA deployments accelerating to 450,000 new households, capturing share from cable incumbents like Comcast in rural markets.

On the cost side, we realized $350 million in synergies from our 2023 Liberty Media acquisition, trimming opex by 7% through shared CDN infrastructure for streaming delivery. Media segment contributions were pivotal too: ad revenues from our FAST channels—think Tubi-like free ad-supported TV—jumped 22% to $650 million, while subscriber growth in GlobalStream hit 1.2 million net adds, pushing total subs to 28 million amid the industry pivot to ad-tier hybrids post-password-sharing crackdowns.

Offsetting this was capex of $1.7 billion, or 22% of revenues, within our guided 21-23% range. We prioritized high-ROI investments: 45% or $765 million went to 5G Ultra Wideband densification, including Open RAN pilots in 15 metros that reduced vendor lock-in costs by 18% versus traditional Huawei/Ericsson stacks. Another 30%—$510 million—funded fiber-to-the-x expansions, adding 2.2 million passings in the U.S. Southeast, positioning us against AT&T's fiber overbuilder ambitions. Media capex, at $250 million, supported edge computing for low-latency 4K/8K streaming and AI-driven content personalization, cutting churn by 15 basis points to 1.1%.

Full-year FCF now tracks to $11.2-11.5 billion, up from prior $10.8-11.2 billion guidance, implying a healthy 12% FCF yield on our current EV. Margins expanded to 28% of revenues, benefiting from EBITDA leverage as wireless equipment sales normalized post the 2022 upgrade supercycle.

Regionally, North America drove 82% of FCF at $2.3 billion, with U.S. 5G penetration now at 65%—ahead of T-Mobile's curve—bolstered by C-band midband rollout. Europe contributed $400 million, flat year-over-year amid regulatory headwinds like the EU's Digital Markets Act squeezing roaming margins, but our Vodafone JV in Germany is ramping FWA to offset. APAC, via our IndiTel subsidiary, surged 35% to $100 million, riding India's Jio-like 5G data explosion, where we added 800,000 subs on sub-$10 ARPU plans.

Now, turning to utilization—discipline here is our North Star, balancing growth, deleveraging, and returns in a high-interest-rate world. Of our $2.8 billion Q3 FCF: 65% or $1.82 billion to net debt reduction, lowering our net leverage to 2.1x EBITDA from 2.4x at year-start. This included $1.2 billion in term loan pre-pays at a blended 4.2% rate, well below current SOFR+ spreads, and $620 million in high-coupon 2024 bonds refinanced into greens at 4.9%. Post-quarter, we're at $42 billion net debt, on track for 2.0x by year-end.

20% or $560 million returned via dividends and buybacks. We declared a $0.65 quarterly dividend, up 5% year-over-year, yielding 6.2% forward, appealing to income investors amid media peers' cuts. Share repurchases totaled $300 million under our $5 billion authorization, retiring 1.2% of shares at an average $48, accretive given our $55+ NAV from spectrum assets.

15% or $420 million reinvested strategically: $250 million into the ongoing AWS Outposts migration for hybrid cloud-media workloads, slashing latency 40% for live sports streaming; $120 million for 3.5 GHz CBRS spectrum in secondary markets; and $50 million seeding 6G R&D with Nokia Bell Labs, focusing on network slicing for enterprise private 5G—think metaverse adjacencies for media AR/VR.

Looking ahead, our FCF strategy positions us uniquely: unlike pure-play telcos like Verizon grappling with legacy copper drags, our media flywheel—30% of EBITDA from content—diversifies cash streams, much like Comcast's NBCUniversal edge. We're guiding FY24 capex to $7.0-7.3 billion, tapering to 18% of revs in FY25 as 5G ROI matures, unlocking $13+ billion FCF potential by 2026. This funds M&A tuck-ins, like regional FWA roll-ups or European content studios, while sustaining 4-6% dividend growth and opportunistic buybacks.

As your CFO, I'm pleased to dive into our commitment to shareholder returns, with a particular focus on dividend sustainability. In the hyper-competitive telecommunications and media landscape—where we're battling spectrum constraints, surging data demand from 5G and streaming, and content wars with the likes of Netflix, Disney, and Warner Bros. Discovery—our balanced capital allocation strategy has delivered consistent value.

First, on our dividend profile: We declared a quarterly dividend of $0.55 per share today, maintaining our annualized payout of $2.20 per share. At today's closing price of $48.50, that translates to an attractive forward yield of 4.5%—well above the S&P 500 Telecom sector average of 3.2% and competitive with media peers like Comcast at 3.1%. Over the past five years, we've grown our dividend at a 6% CAGR, outpacing inflation and matching the 5-7% EPS growth we've delivered through subscriber adds in our 5G wireless segment and bundled streaming services.

Sustainability is rock-solid, underpinned by robust free cash flow generation. For the trailing 12 months, we generated $6.2 billion in FCF—up 12% year-over-year—after $8.4 billion in capex, which was heavily weighted toward our Open RAN 5G deployments and nationwide fiber-to-the-x expansion. This FCF comfortably covers our $2.8 billion annual dividend obligation, providing 2.2x coverage. Our payout ratio stands at 58% of adjusted EPS of $3.78, within our target range of 50-65%, and even more conservatively at 45% of FCF when normalized for one-time 3.5 GHz spectrum auction payments earlier this year.

Leverage metrics further bolster this: Our net debt-to-adjusted EBITDA ratio improved to 2.6x from 2.9x last quarter, thanks to $1.2 billion in deleveraging from asset monetizations, including the sale of non-core tower assets to American Tower for $850 million. This positions us below the investment-grade threshold targeted by peers like Verizon (2.8x) and AT&T (2.9x), giving us ample dry powder amid rising interest rates.

Turning to total shareholder returns, we've returned $4.5 billion over the past 12 months—a 9.2% total yield including dividends and buybacks. Beyond the dividend, we repurchased $1.7 billion in shares under our $3 billion authorization, retiring 35 million shares or 2.1% of float at an average price of $46. This opportunistic program targets our $40-50 buyback window, accretive to EPS given our forward P/E of 12.8x versus the sector's 14.5x.

Regional and strategic insights highlight why this is sustainable long-term. In North America, our core market (85% of revenue), wireless ARPU grew 4% to $58.50 on 5G Ultra Wideband pricing and postpaid net adds of 450,000—fueled by edge computing partnerships with AWS for low-latency gaming and enterprise IoT. Broadband churn dipped to 1.1%, below industry norms, via our 'StreamFiber' bundles integrating Paramount+ and Peacock content, driving 8% RBV growth in media. This segment's 42% EBITDA margin covers 65% of our dividend alone.

Internationally, APAC expansion—via our 40% stake in Singtel's Optus—added $450 million in FCF contribution, with 5G Standalone launches in Australia yielding 15% subscriber growth amid the region's 20%+ data traffic surge. In Europe, regulatory tailwinds from the EU's Gigabit Infrastructure Act are accelerating our fixed wireless access rollout, targeting 2 million homes passed by year-end and offsetting competitive pressure from Vodafone and Orange.

Technical initiatives securing future FCF include virtualized network functions reducing opex by 18% through our Ericsson-led cloud-native core, and AI-driven network slicing for premium 5G services like AR/VR streaming, which we expect to add $500 million in incremental revenue by 2025. We're also pruning low-margin legacy copper assets, projecting $300 million in annual savings phased in over 18 months.

Looking ahead, we reaffirm our full-year FCF guidance of $6.0-6.5 billion, implying sustained 2x+ dividend coverage. Subject to Board approval, we anticipate a 5% dividend hike in Q1 2025, supported by 3-5% EPS growth from organic trends and $400 million in synergies from our recent Liberty Latin America acquisition. Combined with $2 billion in planned buybacks, total returns should exceed 8% yield.

In summary, our dividend isn't just sustainable—it's a cornerstone of value creation in a capex-intensive industry, backed by FCF discipline, strategic M&A, and tech leadership. We're committed to compounding shareholder value while investing in the 5G-media convergence that will define the next decade.

Dr. Raj Patel: Thank you, Maria. I would like to provide an update on our network performance. We have made significant progress in expanding our 5G coverage. Our network reliability metrics continue to improve, and we are seeing increased data usage across our customer base. We are also actively working on enhancing our cybersecurity infrastructure. Our team's dedication to delivering seamless connectivity has been instrumental in achieving these results.

Thank you, Alex. I'll now turn to our network investments, where we're making substantial progress on our 5G deployment while prudently managing capital expenditures to drive long-term shareholder value in both our telecommunications and media segments.

First, on 5G deployment progress: We're thrilled with the momentum we've built this quarter. As of Q3 end, we've achieved 95% 5G coverage across our top 100 U.S. metro markets, up from 85% at year-start, leveraging a mix of sub-6GHz mid-band spectrum—primarily our C-band holdings from the 2021 FCC auction—and mmWave for ultra-high-capacity urban densification. Nationwide, we're at 62% population coverage, with a strong push into suburban and exurban areas via small cells and massive MIMO upgrades. In terms of technology maturity, we've transitioned 45% of our footprint to full Standalone 5G, enabling network slicing for enterprise use cases like private 5G networks for media production studios. This is ahead of our internal roadmap and positions us competitively against peers like Verizon, which reported 60% SA coverage last quarter.

Regionally, performance varies but remains robust. In the U.S. Northeast and West Coast corridors—our highest ARPU markets—we're at 98% coverage with average download speeds exceeding 450 Mbps, thanks to over 15,000 new Massive MIMO radios deployed in partnership with Ericsson. Midwest expansion has accelerated, hitting 75% coverage in key DMAs like Chicago and Detroit, supported by Nokia's AirScale portfolio. Internationally, through our JV with Vodafone in Europe, we've lit up 5G SA in 12 major cities across Germany and the UK, covering 70% of our joint European population and enabling low-latency applications like AR/VR content delivery for our media properties. In Latin America, via our Claro Brazil operations, we're at 40% coverage but growing 30% quarter-over-quarter, focusing on sub-6GHz to address spectrum constraints post the Anatel 3.5GHz auction.

Technically, key initiatives include Open RAN pilots at scale: We've certified and deployed Open RAN on 2,500 sites with Nokia and Samsung, reducing vendor lock-in and projecting 15-20% opex savings over five years. We're also advancing cloud-native core migration, with 5G Core v17.5 live in 20 markets, unlocking Multi-access Edge Computing for media synergies—think sub-10ms latency for our live sports streaming on GlobalStream, which saw 5G-driven session times increase 28% quarter-over-quarter. Fiber backhaul investments have reached 85% of cell sites, critical for handling the 5G traffic surge, which is up 35% year-over-year.

Now, pivoting to capital expenditures: Total capex for the first nine months came in at $11.2 billion, in line with our guidance and representing 18% of trailing twelve-month revenues. Breakdown: 60% or $6.7 billion allocated to Radio Access Network modernization and 5G site builds (including 25,000 new sites and upgrades); 25% or $2.8 billion to transport and backhaul (primarily metro Ethernet and DWDM fiber densification); 10% or $1.1 billion to core and packet core; and the balance to IT/enterprise and spectrum-related initiatives. Full-year capex guidance remains $14.5-15.0 billion, with Q4 weighted toward SA 5G rollout and rural digital divide programs under the BEAD funding umbrella, where we've secured $2.3 billion in preliminary allocations.

Strategically, these investments are yielding clear returns. 5G subscribers now represent 28% of our postpaid mobile base, up 150 basis points quarter-over-quarter, driving a 4.2% ARPU uplift from premium plans bundling unlimited 5G with our media content (e.g., ad-supported tiers for Paramount+ integration). Churn in 5G segments is down 20 basis points to 0.85%, and fixed wireless access trials have onboarded 150,000 households at gigabit speeds, cannibalizing legacy DSL while boosting broadband EBITDA margins to 52%. Looking ahead, we're allocating 5% of 2025 capex—about $750 million—to 6G R&D and AI-orchestrated networks, partnering with Qualcomm on O-RAN Alliance projects. This positions us to capture the $1T global 5G enterprise opportunity by 2030, per GSMA forecasts, while enhancing media delivery—ultra-HD streaming, cloud gaming, and metaverse experiences—with edge caching reducing transit costs by 22%.

In summary, our disciplined 5G spend is transforming our network into a media-grade asset, balancing coverage expansion with ROI discipline. We're on track for 85% nationwide coverage by year-end, with capex efficiency improving to $1,200 per covered household.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. In order to allow for as many questions as possible, please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. Our first question comes from John Smith with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you discuss the competitive landscape and your strategy for 5G monetization?

Alex Rivera: Certainly, John. The competitive landscape remains intense, with peers like T-Mobile and Verizon pushing aggressive pricing and coverage. Our strategy for 5G monetization centers on premium bundles that leverage our Ultra5G network slicing and partnerships, such as with Apple and Epic Games, driving ARPU uplift of over 2% as we've seen this quarter. We're differentiating through low-latency applications for gaming, XR, and enterprise IoT, while our Open RAN deployments keep costs in check. This has allowed us to outpace competitors in postpaid net adds and maintain industry-leading churn.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Davis with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Davis: Hi, thanks for taking my question. What are your expectations for subscriber growth in the next quarter, and how will that impact ARPU?

Maria Chen: We anticipate continued momentum with about 1 million total net adds in Q4, including 600,000 postpaid wireless and 300,000 broadband, driven by holiday promotions and fiber passings growth. This will positively impact ARPU, which we expect to grow 1.5-2% quarter-over-quarter through 5G Advanced uptake and bundling with GlobalStream, offsetting any promotional drag and supporting our full-year ARPU stability around $58.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mike Thompson with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Thompson: Can you provide an update on your fiber deployment plans and the expected ROI on those investments?

Dr. Raj Patel: Absolutely, Mike. Our FiberFast network now passes 35 million locations, with plans to hit 50 million by 2026 through $1.8 billion in annual capex. Take rates are up to 52%, and we're gaining share in Sun Belt markets against Comcast. Expected ROI exceeds 25%, fueled by gigabit symmetrical speeds, FWA synergies, and BEAD funding. Early markets show EBITDA margins over 50%, with payback periods under 4 years.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. Alex, would you like to provide closing remarks?

Alex Rivera: Thank you. In closing, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain confident in our ability to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value. Thank you for your time and interest in GlobalCom Inc.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
